A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same ORIGEN work and provide readable text, equations, figures, tables, and appendices. Retained content can be matched reliably across the added sections and renumbering.

before.justification: V2 reports original ORIBENCH evaluations, the toy experiment in Figure 2, computational measurements, and the human preference study in Table 2.

after.justification: V3 retains these original results and adds hyperparameter experiments, additional baseline comparisons, and layout-to-image and depth-guided generation results in Tables 8–10.

M1.justification: Appendix L adds task-specific reward configurations: GroundingDINO supplies bounding-box guidance, and DepthAnything-V2 supplies depth guidance. These extend the conditioning and reward components while retaining the orientation method, Langevin updates, and adaptive time-rescaling algorithm.

E1.justification: V3 extends evaluation beyond orientation grounding to layout-to-image generation on HRS-Spatial and depth-guided generation using ORIBENCH-Single images. These introduce spatial-layout and depth-map conditioning requirements. Appendix K also introduces DDPO training data drawn from OrientAnything and Cap3D; the original orientation benchmarks remain.

E2.justification: Appendix K and Table 9 add DDPO, SV3D, and MV-Adapter to the ORIBENCH-Single training-based comparison, previously limited to Zero-1-to-3 and C3DW. This substantially broadens the evaluated comparator families. The original comparisons are retained.

E3.justification: New protocols include controlled monitor-parameter sweeps, DDPO fine-tuning using 50k orientations paired with captions and textual orientation conditioning, and separate 100-example layout and depth evaluations. The latter introduce mIoU/HRS and AbsRel measurements. Existing ORIBENCH evaluation settings and the user-study protocol are retained.

E4.justification: Appendix J and Table 8 add a focused sensitivity study of the monitor slope k and step-size bounds, holding other settings fixed. This supplements the existing adaptive-versus-fixed-step comparison and convergence analysis by testing sensitivity to the monitor's parameter choices.

E5.justification: Neither version provides repeated-run variability, seed counts, confidence intervals, or formal significance tests for the benchmark scores. The added tables continue the existing point-estimate reporting practice, and user-study participant and filtering information remains unchanged.

E6.justification: Existing numerical results are retained, while Tables 8–10 add sensitivity, baseline, and new-task results. For example, layout mIoU is 0.344 for ORIGEN versus 0.244/0.287 for FreeDoM/ReNO; depth AbsRel is 4.62 versus 6.34/6.67. Text-to-image scores are mixed. Figure 9 adds corresponding qualitative examples; these are new comparisons, not improvements over v2 under changed settings.

T1.justification: The mathematical formulation, Proposition 1, and derivations in Appendices A–C are retained. V3 adds no new theorem, proof, formal assumption, or substantive mathematical correction.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction contributions, and conclusion retain the same claims about zero-shot multi-object orientation grounding, reward-guided Langevin sampling, adaptive convergence, and comparative performance. The additional appendix evidence does not redefine these central claims.

C2.justification: Appendices J and L newly interpret the results as showing non-fragile monitor hyperparameters and applicability across different rewards. Appendix L.2 also asserts broadly superior image quality, although Table 10's text-to-image scores are mixed. Existing discriminator-dependence and back-facing-generation limitations are retained.

D1.justification: V3 newly discloses coarse-grid-search selection of the retained monitor defaults, DDPO prompt and training-data construction, target-view selection from SV3D's 21 and MV-Adapter's six outputs, and reward/evaluation models for the new tasks. Existing ORIGEN implementation details, hardware information, and project-page access information remain unchanged.

R1.justification: New citations and appendix descriptions cover SV3D, MV-Adapter, Objaverse/Cap3D, HRS-Bench, Salience DETR, and DepthAnything-V2. DDPO's underlying paper was already cited in v2 and is relocated in the bibliography. These additions broaden the comparison context without substantially rewriting the main research positioning.

P1.justification: The main narrative and existing appendices remain largely unchanged. V3 adds acknowledgments, a conference footer, and explanatory Appendices J–L; former Appendices J/K become M/N. It also introduces an unresolved citation in Section 2. There is no extensive rewriting or reorganization of the retained exposition.

P2.justification: V3 adds three tables for sensitivity, extended baselines, and the two new tasks, plus a qualitative layout/depth figure. Existing displays and examples are retained; former Figures 9–10 become Figures 10–11. Other changes mainly involve page reflow and small labeling adjustments.

improvement.justification: The new sensitivity checks and additional trained baselines strengthen empirical support, while the layout and depth experiments broaden demonstrated applicability. However, Appendix L.2 overstates image-quality superiority: Table 10 gives ReNO higher CLIP, VQA, and PickScore on depth generation. The added evidence provides a limited net improvement despite this interpretive weakness.
